What are the specifications of the NVIDIA H100 SXM GPU?

The NVIDIA H100 SXM is built on the Hopper architecture with 80 GB of HBM3 memory delivering 3.35 TB/s of bandwidth. It features 4th Generation Tensor Cores providing 3,958 TFLOPS of FP8 and 1,979 TFLOPS of FP16/BF16 compute with sparsity. It uses SXM5 form factor, connects via NVLink at 900 GB/s plus PCIe Gen5, supports up to 7 MIG partitions (10 GB each), has a configurable TDP of up to 700W, and includes a hardware Transformer Engine.

How does dedicated GPU hosting cost compare to per-token APIs like OpenRouter or Together AI?

Under dedicated GPU hosting with vLLM, continuous batching allows multiple requests to share GPU time. While serverless per-token APIs ($0.20 to $0.88 per 1M tokens) are cheaper for low, sporadic usage (e.g. <5,000 queries/day), dedicated GPUs become dramatically more cost-effective as traffic scales: 1) Llama 3.1 8B on an L4 at concurrency C=16 achieves ~420 tokens/sec, costing ~$0.029 per 1M tokens (8.5x cheaper than per-token APIs). 2) Llama 3.1 70B FP8 on an H100 SXM at C=64 achieves ~1280 tokens/sec, costing ~$0.076 per 1M tokens (over 11x cheaper than APIs charging $0.88/1M tokens).

How do you calculate the exact VRAM required to deploy an LLM on Inferxe?

VRAM is calculated using: Total_Peak_VRAM = Weights_GB + KV_Cache_GB + Runtime_Overhead_GB. 1) Weights: ParameterCount_B × BytesPerParam (FP16/BF16 = 2 bytes, FP8 = 1 byte, INT4 = 0.5 bytes). 2) KV Cache: (Context_Tokens / 1024) × Batch_Size × (KV_Factor_MB / 1024), scaling with sequence length and concurrency. 3) Overhead: ~2.5 GB reserved for CUDA context, activations, and vLLM memory buffers. To prevent out-of-memory errors, the workload must strictly fit within the 90% usable VRAM ceiling (Total_VRAM × 0.90).
